desk.headline: HEPS up 25.7% to 587c as Safaricom is consolidated; revenue up 25.6% to R102.5bn; medium-term targets confirmed
results: Headline earnings per share rose 25.7% to 587c, helped by consolidating Safaricom as a subsidiary from 30 June 2026.
Revenue grew 25.6% to R102.5bn; service revenue rose 29.4% to R85.1bn, or 13.3% on a like-for-like (pro forma) basis.
EBITDA jumped 40% to R42.7bn (18% pro forma); South Africa's EBITDA margin was 37.4% and its revenue rose 2.1% to R45.8bn, with prepaid back to growth.
Egypt service revenue grew 36.3% in local currency; Safaricom service revenue rose 13.1% and its EBITDA 27.5%.
The interim dividend rose 7.6% to 355c, reflecting the revised payout policy of at least 65% of headline earnings.

guidance.summary: Vodacom says it is tracking ahead of its medium-term targets, which were upgraded in July: double-digit service revenue growth and early-teens EBITDA growth. It gives no figure for the full year.

items.prior: early teens (raised from double-digit in Jul 2026)

points: CEO Shameel Joosub said South African data traffic growth is strong and speeding up, as customers buy much bigger bundles at sharper prices.

He said Vodacom is confident of winning its appeal against the Kenyan High Court ruling that voided the purchase of the government's 15% Safaricom stake, and that the Kenyan government backs the appeal.
Fintech is a key growth push, extending lending, investment, merchant services and insurance into more markets.
Raising smartphone take-up (now 69.8%) was stressed as the route to bringing more people into digital services.
call.source: EWN (10 Nov 2026) and TechAfrica News (10 Nov 2026) coverage of the results presentation

watch: The Kenyan Court of Appeal ruling on the Safaricom stake — losing it would cut Vodacom's holding to about 40% and end consolidation.
Debt levels after the Safaricom purchase and the effect of the lower dividend payout.
Whether South African service revenue growth picks up from about 2%.
